description_full: Bending Spoons S.p.A., through its subsidiaries, acquires and transforms digital businesses in the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, Poland, Canada, Japan, Australia, France, Brazil, Italy, and internationally. The company designs and develops software and platforms that support acquisitions, transformations, and ongoing optimizations. The company's portfolio includes AOL, which operates an email service, news portal, and search engine; Brightcove, which provides video hosting, management, and streaming solutions for enterprises; Eventbrite, which delivers event creation, ticketing, and discovery services for organizers and attendees; Evernote, a productivity suite that supports note-taking and knowledge management for individuals and teams; Harvest, which offers time-tracking and invoicing software for freelancers and professional services firms; Komoot, which provides route planning and navigation tools; Remini, a consumer-focused image and video enhancement and generation application; StreamYard, which provides video recording and multi-destination live-streaming tools for creators and businesses; Vimeo, which provides video hosting, management, and streaming solutions for consumers and enterprises; WeTransfer, which enables digital file storage and distribution for individuals and businesses; and Tractive, which delivers solutions for monitoring the location and health of pets. The company was founded in 2013 and is based in Milan, Italy.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 1K people. Revenue per employee of $1.5M ranks in the top quartile among Technology peers. Each employee generates $166K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $32K per employee reflects an ownership culture. R&D investment of 11% of revenue (significant) signals commitment to product development and talent.
financial_summary: Bending Spoons S.p.A. is a large-cap technology business with a $27.0B market cap on $2.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +160% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 13% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically. Gross margins of 64% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $290M in free cash flow — roughly 11 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 12.95× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 4.0× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 1.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Net dilution runs at 1.0% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 21% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
